transcript.answer: No, not any more. An `error` frame must never clear `busy`. Issue #191 changed the rule that issue 044 had set. Under 044 the client cleared `busy` on `stream_end`, on an `error` frame, or on socket close. Engine change #148 (issue 139) made `stream_end` the single terminal frame, sent once per accepted message whether or not an error occurred. A measured probe found an unrelated `INVALID_MESSAGE` error landing between two `entry_delta` frames of a healthy stream. A client that cleared `busy` on that error would drop the typing indicator and unlock the composer mid-answer. So `busy` now clears only on `stream_end` or socket close. The `error` frame still sets `state.error`. Spec FR-013 says an `error` frame alone never clears `busy`. It is validated by the test 'stays busy through a SERVER_ERROR frame and clears only on the stream_end after it'.

judgements.reason: The answer says no, cites the INVALID_MESSAGE error arriving between entry_delta frames of a healthy stream, identifies stream_end as the single terminal frame sent once per accepted message, and states busy clears only on stream_end or socket close.
